//: Railway deployment for the PUBLIC WEBSITE (apps/site), Little Pearls' own littlepearls.org.nz.
A SECOND FILE, AND WHY THAT IS NOT OPTIONAL
railway.json is a single-service manifest with `startCommand: npm run start -w @ece/web`.
A second Railway service that reads it would boot the PLATFORM, health-check it happily on
/api/health, and serve the app that holds children's records on the marketing domain. That
failure is silent — a green deploy pointing at the wrong application.
So the second service must be configured with this file as its config path (Settings ->
Config-as-code -> railway.site.json), and its root directory must stay the REPO ROOT.
docs/deploy-railway.md already records the root-directory version of this trap: Railway's
workspace detection offers a service per workspace with root dir apps/<x>, and a config file
at the repo root is then silently ignored.
WHY A SEPARATE SERVICE RATHER THAN ONE CONTAINER SERVING BOTH
One Next process cannot serve two apps, but the real reason is the boundary. This container
holds NO service-role key. CORRECTED 2026-08-07: it used to say 'no Supabase credential of
any kind — apps/site has no @supabase/* dependency at all', which stopped being true when
the careers form was built. It holds the ANON key, whose whole capability is one
void-returning definer function; anon has no table grant anywhere and review:security fails
the build at high severity if that changes. Nixpacks bakes every Railway variable into the image as
ARG/ENV, so image access is variable access; keeping the public-facing, unauthenticated
surface in an image with no database credentials in it is the whole point.
ON NAMING: docs/deploy-railway.md says not to name a service or a custom domain after the
first customer, because the platform is pooled-tenant and one customer's name on it would be
wrong the moment a second signs up. That rule does not apply here and its inverse does —
this service IS Little Pearls' website, single-tenant by decision, on their own domain.
`build:site` — core, then site. NOT the root `npm run build`, and the reason is the whole
point of this service existing.
The root build chain includes `-w @ece/web`, and `next build` on the platform needs
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY at BUILD time — Next inlines
them into the client bundle. So a site service running the root build would need Supabase
variables set on it, Nixpacks would bake them into this image as ARG/ENV, and the public
marketing container would ship with database credentials in its layers. That is exactly the
property this service was separated to avoid.
It is a named script in the root package.json rather than an inline command here, so it is
runnable locally, reviewable in a diff, and cannot quietly diverge from something CI could
also run. `apps/site` depends on @ece/core, @supabase/supabase-js, and ONE module of
@ece/api (recruitment.ts, whose only imports are types) — never @ece/api's index, so the
public container cannot construct a service-role client.
The workspace flag matters: `npm run start` at the root has no start script, and
`cd apps/site && npm start` loses npm's workspace symlink for @ece/core.
